title: Godot Foundation welcomes Manus as Platinum Sponsor
description: We’d like to welcome Manus as a Platinum Sponsor of the Godot Foundation. Their contribution helps keep Godot free, open, and in constant development for everyone, and we truly appreciate it. Here is a message from them: A message from Manus: AI is lowering the technical barriers to making games, but a tool is only ever a tool. A good game is one you and your friends love to play over and over, and that comes from your sense of how it should feel, the little details, and the odd ideas only you would have. From here on, what’s rare isn’t the ability to build, it’s knowing what you want to build. Godot has done more than almost anyone to put real game-making tools in everyone’s hands: an open-source engine shaped by its community and kept going by contributors and paid developers who care about it. We’re proud to support that work, and we hope more people who make their first game with Manus will go on to explore what they can create with Godot. — Tao Zhang, Co-founder & CPO, Manus AI Manus is the world’s first general AI agent that turns ideas into finished work. To learn more, read the Game Dev blog post: Introducing Game Dev: Enabling Everyone to Make the Games They Want to Play.

title: JetBrains Renews its Platinum Sponsorship of the Godot Foundation
description: We’re happy to share that JetBrains has renewed its Platinum sponsorship of the Godot Foundation for 2027. JetBrains first joined as a Platinum sponsor in August 2025. Alongside the sponsorship, JetBrains has kept expanding Godot support in JetBrains Rider. Over the past year, Rider has grown to cover GDScript, C#, and C++ GDExtensions in one IDE, and it’s free for non-commercial use, including hobby projects, learning, open-source, and content creation. Here’s what Rider brings to Godot developers: GDScript support: Code completion, Find Usages, the Rename refactoring, inspections, and a formatter. You can drag nodes from Scene Preview into a script to insert their paths or generate @onready and @export variables. Debugging and testing: Debug GDScript and C# from Rider, including specific scenes and tool scripts, and debug both languages at the same time in mixed projects. C# tests run with the Chickensoft GoDotTest runner. Native development: Build C++ GDExtensions with CMake, and inspect Godot’s native types in the debugger with godot-cpp.natvis on Linux and macOS. Addon development: Project templates for Godot games, assets, and editor plugins, ready for publishing on the Godot Asset Store. Coming in Rider 2026.3: Navigation from $Node and %UniqueNode references to scene nodes, Find Usages for signal connections made through Callable, and the Remote Scene tree and node inspector while debugging C#. These are available now in the Early Access Program. For the full overview, including how Mega Crit develops Slay the Spire 2 with Rider, read the JetBrains blog post: From GDScript to GDExtensions: One IDE for Your Godot Code. About JetBrains Rider and Godot JetBrains has been investing in Godot support for several years. Rider provides code insight and debugging for GDScript and C#, scene and resource navigation, and C++ tooling for GDExtensions and engine work. The official JetBrains Rider Integration addon in the Godot Asset Store connects Rider to the Godot…

title: Godot Showcase - Sovereign Tower
description: .paul { color: #aa77e2; }.lisa { color: #40b99f; } Today, Paul Mozet (Lead Programmer on Sovereign Tower) and Lisa Garnier (Narrative Design and Technical Artist on Sovereign Tower) from Wild Wits Games tell us about their experience developing their latest Godot game: Sovereign Tower. Sovereign Tower is a story-rich Round Table management RPG where you recruit eccentric Knights, assign quests and balance egos whilst carving out your kingdom’s destiny. The game is already out on Steam for Windows and Linux. Can you tell us a little bit about your game? Paul Mozet (Lead Programmer on Sovereign Tower): Sovereign Tower is a round table manager RPG, mostly narrative, where you are the new Sovereign of a kingdom. You will have to recruit knights at your round table and dispatch them through the kingdom to answer the grievances of your people and the other counties’ representatives that will come to see you, while managing the ego of all of those eccentric characters. And if anything goes awry, you can count on the demon of the tower to go back in time and try to handle things in a different way! How did you get your start in game development? And how did it grow into a full-time position? Paul: A composer friend of mine, Pierrick Veillerobe, motivated me to do a Ludum Dare game jam with him while I was studying computer science back in 2021. I loved the experience and we made a few more in the year after. At the same time, I had the opportunity to meet Corto and François, the founders of Wild Wits Games and they welcomed me in 2022 to do a two months internship as a programmer on Aetheris, the first game of the studio. As the internship went well, they offered me a full-time position at the studio, as a programmer, an offer that I immediately accepted. Lisa Garnier (Narrative Design and Technical Artist on Sovereign Tower): I first started exploring interactive media while I was at art school, graduating in 2020. I then switched to a computer science program to develop…

title: Ready for XREAL AURA
description: XREAL AURA, the first optical see-through glasses on Android XR, is here and Godot is part of the launch lineup! Develop natively on spatial computing glasses Download the Godot editor and its companion app on the XREAL AURA, and develop, export, and publish spatial Godot games and apps natively on XREAL AURA. The Godot editor on XREAL AURA provides the features that you’d come to expect and love on desktop within a multi-window spatial workspace that goes with you. Download Godot editor on Google Play: Build spatial games and apps Godot continues the trend of being one of the lightest, most flexible, and best engines for XR development by delivering a plethora of new features to provide developers access to the newest Android XR capabilities available on XREAL AURA. This includes support for the new OpenXR Spatial Containers, which are system-managed volumes in which applications can display spatial content, similar to how traditional applications draw 2D content within windows on a desktop. On XREAL AURA, Godot spatial games and apps come alive right on your table, anchored exactly where you place it, with hand tracking and a low-latency spatial display that make every move feel natural. These new spatial capabilities lower the barrier of entry for developers to build new spatial games and apps, or port existing 3D games. Porting DOGWALK to XREAL AURA To showcase the new OpenXR Spatial Containers on XREAL AURA, and the ease through which developers can port their 3D games to Spatial Containers, the Godot Foundation in partnership with Blender Studio and W4 Games, is working on a spatial port of DOGWALK to XREAL AURA. This project builds on the ongoing collaboration between the Godot Foundation and W4 Games to expand Godot’s Android XR support. Working closely together, the teams have tackled the engineering challenges and optimizations involved in bringing the spatial version of DOGWALK to XREAL AURA in a relatively short time, and are now hard at work polishing…

title: Godot XR Community Game Jam VI
description: The sixth Godot XR Community Game Jam ran from 21 September 2026 until 5 October 2026. We had 85 participants join, who submitted 28 games. Down from 98 participants but up from 22 games last jam. The quality of the entries however has risen sharply. The theme of this game jam was “Adrift”. The whole top 10 is worth checking out and even beyond are some real gems, but as always we’re counting down the top 5: No 5. Balloon Dino Death Dome by Kimau This entry has you take control of a balloon where you physically need to pull on levers to control the balloon. Well, for as far as you have control because for the most part, different air currents take over. Those air currents are brilliantly visualised and animated with tiny particles. A cannon mounted on the balloon has you shooting targets to score points. No 4. Tether Charge Express VR by UltraGravityLabs This entry has you trying to stay in front of a storm. Through a unique control mechanism, you control a drone on the end of a tether that gathers electricity from the storm to power your craft. It becomes a balancing act between collecting energy, evading the storm, and recharging your craft. No 3. Build a Lighthouse VR by Bauxite This entry is a very impressive physics-based tower stacking game. You find yourself on a little island in the middle of an ocean, with all sorts of flotsam drifting ashore. As you do, you pick up the flotsam, and try and build the highest tower. The physics interaction in this game is sublime; it is a real challenge building a tower where every new piece can upset the balance. This is hours of fun! No 2. Balloons Adrift VR by simenhs This deceptively simple entry has you shooting balloons out of the air. Gunplay in VR is always satisfying but what sets this apart is that at the start of the game, you only get a few seconds to shoot. With each balloon successfully popped, you get a few dollars to spend. After each round, you can buy upgrades, be it additional time, more dollars per…

title: Optimizing CPU-side Rendering Code
description: I want to give people a little bit of insight into what the optimization process looks like for Godot’s renderer. From the outside, rendering optimization can look a little bit like black magic. I want to show a few examples of some optimizations that we did this year to highlight that optimizing rendering code isn’t as scary as it sounds. Bottlenecks In this article I will only be looking at optimizing CPU code. When working on renderers, you need to be very careful about optimizing code both for the CPU and for the GPU, because your ultimate performance will be dictated by the slower of the two processors. No amount of CPU optimization will save you from inefficient shaders. In writing a renderer you also make tradeoffs all the time to benefit one or the other. For example, batching in 2D is a technique that hurts GPU performance a little, but improves CPU performance a lot. Since 2D games tend to get CPU bottlenecked before they get GPU bottlenecked, batching ends up being a net positive in most cases. Conversely, 3D games tend to be GPU bottlenecked more often, so in Godot we do our occlusion culling on the CPU in order to take some of the load off the GPU. Regardless of your ultimate balance between CPU and GPU work, it is always beneficial to optimize the engine since any optimization to the engine leaves more space for game developers to use the CPU and GPU and saves battery power for power-constrained platforms. Methodology The process of optimizing CPU performance roughly looks like: Identify the performance bottlenecks/hotspots Understand why the bottleneck is where it is Investigate solutions Re-measure performance Repeat Identify the performance bottlenecks This is the hardest part of performance optimization. When your game or application starts running poorly it can be difficult to track down exactly why. Often once you see where the poor performance is coming from, you immediately understand why performance is bad. This is often the case when you…
